question: The Rodalies suburban rail network in Catalonia, whose infrastructure and management depend on the state, is experiencing recurrent incidents, service interruptions and widespread delays affecting hundreds of thousands of users.

The situation has recently worsened, with incidents linked to deteriorating infrastructure, which have led to suspensions of service for several days and, in the most serious case, the death of a driver. EU law imposes clear obligations on railway infrastructure managers.

Directive 2012/34/EU requires managers to ensure the maintenance, upgrading and quality of service, while Directive (EU) 2016/798 stipulates that a safety management system should be in place covering the design, maintenance and safe operation of the infrastructure. In view of this state of affairs: 1.
Has the Commission assessed whether Spain’s state-owned railway infrastructure manager – Adif – is complying with its obligation to maintain and upgrade the Rodalies network?
Does the Commission think that the recurrent deficiencies demonstrate a failure to comply with safety management and infrastructure maintenance requirements?
If there is a lack of compliance, what steps does the Commission envisage taking to ensure the safety of the suburban rail network service?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (28.4.2026) Under the EU railway safety Directive (EU) 2016/7981, the responsibility to assess the status of the infrastructure of the Rodalies network falls under responsibility of the national safety authority, in this case the Agencia Estatal de Seguridad Ferroviaria (AESF).

If the AESF, in the framework of its supervision role, finds that an infrastructure manager no longer satisfies the conditions for its safety authorisation, according to Art 17.5 of the Rail Safety Directive it shall restrict or revoke that authorisation, giving reasons for its decision.

In case the Commission becomes aware of a potential lack of compliance, it may request to the European Union Railway Agency (ERA) to provide evidence on the state of implementation and application of Union legislation on railway safety and interoperability, according to Art 33(5) of Regulation 2016/796 on the European Union Agency for Railway2.

On that basis, the Commission could take further steps, using the appropriate instruments under the Rail Safety Directive that aim to guarantee the highest levels of safety and ensure that each actor fulfils its responsibility towards it.
